_about: Les features livrées au TEMPS COURANT — bascule IA, versions 0.6.x, depuis le 2026-08-03. Les features antérieures (l'éditeur d'arbre) sont dans features_history.0.5.json, qui n'est PAS en lecture obligatoire. Ce fichier-ci l'est.

features.goal: Fix the adventure dossier as the single persisted format — a versioned schema (schema:1, three grouped roots canon/monde/charpente), a validator that refuses in French what is not playable, deep-freeze on import, round-trip import/export, and a reference dossier — so the fifteen following features (editor and play engine) have a stable contract to consume.
key_architecture_choices: types.ts is split into rules types (survive, consumed by src/player/) vs tree.ts (the doomed tree model) — the physical barrier that makes KR-167 (no Book<->Dossier converter, ever) verifiable by a test-grep rather than a comment.

Validation rules are TABLE data (tables.ts), never if/switch cascades (KR-117): one path-expanding walker (sitesDe) reads RACINES/CHAMPS_REQUIS/ENUMERES_FERMES/LISTES_REQUISES/REFERENCES_SIMPLES/CHEMINS_DE_DELTAS/FAMILLES_DE_CONDITIONS. Extending the schema is adding rows.

Conditions (…_expr) are a persisted JSON tree (ExprNode, four French operators) with NO parser — validateExpr + collectRefs only — driven by a closed PREDICATES registry (7 entries) that renders as widgets, never free syntax (KR-168).

Effects (…) are a closed DELTAS registry (4 reference-only slots: donner_objet/retirer_objet/reveler_indice/atteindre_jalon); every integer-magnitude delta is deliberately excluded until docs/REGLES-DU-JEU.md poses the rule (KR-130), reopened doc -> golden test -> code, in that order.

A DESTINATION_DES_CHAMPS table (ia/moteur/auteur) declares the AUDIENCE of every terminal field, closed by couverture.test.ts's full-depth corruption sweep over the real fixture — the instrument that would have caught monde fields silently reaching a future AI-context assembler.
validateDossier is pure (never freezes its argument) and deep-freezes a JSON-cloned COPY on success — the only Object.freeze site in the module, test-grepped to stay unique (KR-166).

it5: a SECOND fixture (dossier-reference.json, six personnages, five lieux) proves schema sufficiency by real narrative construction rather than enriching dossier-minimal.json, which seven other test suites read and partially pin — a seven-suite blast radius for zero benefit.

it5: the suffisance checklist is a local test table (BRANCHES: {nom, predicat}) so every failure names its branch (KR-157) instead of a silent boolean — the substitute proof-of-slice when the iteration ships no screen (KR-156).
lessons_learned: A number cited in a plan must state its PREDICATE, not just its count, and must be re-measured every time it is quoted rather than copy-pasted forward — the types.ts->tree.ts import-line count (KR-159) and the 'validate.ts <= 650 lines' threshold that acquired authority purely by repetition without ever having a source (KR-176) both cost review time for the same underlying mistake.

A registry indexed by an untrusted value must use its own hasOwnProperty guard, never `in` or a bare index test — every plain object inherits Object.prototype, so 'toString' in REGISTRY is true and REGISTRY['toString'] is a function; a cast (`as`) placed right after a weak guard is exactly where tsc stops protecting (BUG-053, KR-175).

A property asserted only in a docstring ('pure', 'total', 'the only call site') is an intention, not a contract until a test pins it — three of four PR-review majors across the feature were exactly this shape, including validateDossier's docstring claiming purity while actually freezing its caller's argument (BUG-038, KR-169).

When a total/defensive traversal silently skips a branch to stay total, what it stops visiting needs its own table, not a comment — three non-optional array fields passed validation absent (BUG-049), and a non-object list element passed silently for the same reason (BUG-050) — both closed by dedicated tables (LISTES_REQUISES, LISTES_A_ELEMENTS_STRUCTURES) rather than widening the walker.

Two agents never work in parallel on the same uncommitted tree once either mutates files — an orchestrator ran an integrator and a QA-mode-B pass concurrently and the QA's legitimate cache-restore (git checkout) wiped 409 lines the integrator was mid-review on (BUG-045, KR-172).

specification.json's resolved_decisions is a write-heavy, append-only section with no automatic ceiling; once code ships AND its revue.md carries the reasoning, an entry compacts to its arbitration sentence + a pointer — the same content duplicated in a production docstring (deltas.ts, predicates.ts, tables.ts) is doubly safe to compact, since it survives in the more durable location.
